overview.goal: Build an externally hosted Wallboard-connected application for an end customer or partner using their chosen frontend, backend, database and hosting.
audience: End customers building applications for themselves
overview.source: Public, versioned integration code, optional Vue components, plain TypeScript and Vue examples, and a Node/SQLite example.
overview.runtime: Each runtime user authenticates through the application's own Wallboard OAuth flow. Wallboard API permissions and application database permissions both apply.
overview.capabilityBoundary: MCP supplies authoring guidance and ordinary authenticated API knowledge. The builder owns source, preview, deployment and artifacts. A Custom UI is an externally hosted web application; uploadable signage widget packages use custom_app_guide.

workflow: Resolve purpose, actors, read/write operations, customer scope, visual identity, target device/surface, application-owned records and hosting/source ownership.
Clone the returned public repository and check out the returned sourceCommit so the guide and source match.
Read AGENTS.md, README.md and the relevant docs; run npm ci and npm run check.
Call get_current_user before authorized customer API work. Use api_howto for verified operations and get_branding for authorized branding; retain normal permissions.
Choose a browser-only app for direct Wallboard operations, or add a backend/database for application-owned workflow state, jobs or server-side credentials.
Use npm run build, then npm run new-app -- <vue|vanilla> <new-directory> for a standalone editable project. Its vendored SDK requires no published npm package.
Reuse connection code and platform components; adapt presentation to the application's brand and workflow. Other frameworks can use the same browser core or OAuth/REST contract.
Validate using synthetic fixtures and inspect the actual UI. Perform live writes only when explicitly authorized against designated test records.
Deploy through the chosen provider's actual process and prove its callback/runtime/storage requirements before describing it as supported.

authentication.browser: createWallboardClient handles OAuth discovery, optional public-client registration, PKCE, one-use callback state, tab-local sessions, single-flight rotating refresh and a verified /api/v2/user/me profile.
authentication.configuration: Use a configured public clientId when DCR is unavailable. Register the exact callback URI. Default callbacks use the origin; the entrypoint must handle that URL.
authentication.session: Use one client per application/server. Default sessionStorage is tab-local; shared storage requires coordinated refresh. Never put a confidential client secret or the builder's MCP token in frontend source.
authentication.authority: Verified API responses establish identity. Decoded JWT display hints never establish authorization. The app backend validates the runtime user's token independently.
authentication.backend: Use createWallboardValidator with a configured trusted server. Its online /me validation follows no redirects and caches no identity by default.
authentication.localVerification: JWKS-only validation needs a verified signing-key format and explicit issuer/audience/key refresh/revocation policy. Check the deployed version; resource audience behavior must be verified rather than inferred.

api.contractSource: Use the existing api_howto, target /v3/api-docs and public API reference for endpoint/body contracts. Typed kit helpers are selected fields, not a second complete schema.
api.helpers: Authenticated transport, explicit forCustomer(customerId), WB/FIELDS/entity subsets, WBQL, pagination, datasource and media helpers.
api.tenantScope: Generic tenant requests need an explicit customerId; instance:true is a deliberate server-wide operation. Global admins select a customer before tenant queries.
api.permissions: Wallboard enforces role, customer, team and read-only restrictions. Preserve 403 outcomes; do not search for a bypass.
api.writes: Verify the actual write contract, replacement/cascade behavior and requested user intent. No automatic retry of uncertain network writes.
api.ui: Use loading/empty/error/forbidden states and discard superseded customer/filter requests. Branding is an explicit application input.

backend.example: examples/node-notes provides Node HTTP and parameterized SQLite CRUD scoped to configured server, customer and user.
backend.authorization: resolveCustomerScope denies global-admin database access unless an application-owned allowlist authorizes the requested customer. The example write policy is disabled by default.
backend.storage: The app owns its database schema, retention and access rules. Use a durable database supported by the provider; an ephemeral SQLite file is not production persistence.
backend.sessionBoundary: The shipped backend accepts bearer tokens per request. A cookie-session BFF requires a complete callback, secure session, CSRF and logout implementation.
backend.adaptation: Other backend languages or provider runtimes can implement the same validated /me identity and application data boundary; Node is an executable reference.

embedding.standalone: Prove standalone login and hosting first.
embedding.frameRequirements: Verify response frame policy, the specific Wallboard surface's sandbox, browser storage and interactive input. CMS and signage frames have different capabilities.
embedding.login: The current kit requires top-level sign-in and rejects framed signIn. Popup/callback handoff is a separate integration that must validate origin/state.
embedding.productBoundary: The guide adds no configurable CMS menu/panel or new signage surface. Use an existing verified URL flow, or implement that product feature separately.
embedding.evidence: A header check or successful build does not prove end-to-end iframe OAuth.

required: Editable source and exact kit revision
Validation results and explicit unverified runtime behavior
delivery.publishing: Deploy through the selected provider with authorized ownership. Git source publication, npm package publication and deployed hosting are separate outcomes.
delivery.sourcePrivacy: Use synthetic fixtures. Never include runtime tokens, the builder's MCP credentials, private customer application source or private server registries.

checklist: SDK and generated project type-check and build; meaningful auth/customer/database tests pass.
Inspect signed-out, loading, empty, error, long-name and mobile UI states.
Prove OAuth callback, refresh, logout policy and rejected/expired credentials on the deployed origin before claiming live login works.
Prove customer scope, forbidden behavior and any application database isolation.
Confirm consequential writes against verified contracts and designated test records.
Prove provider routing, runtime and durable storage assumptions.
Report embedding as verified only after the actual Wallboard iframe/login flow passes.

finalAnswerContract: Return editable source location, exact kit revision, what was built, startup/build/configuration steps, validation outcomes and actual preview/deployment URL. Clearly identify live login, provider/database durability and iframe behaviors that remain unverified.
